prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Company news: IT hardware, networking, data-center and power-equipment.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Every material company-specific news item for US-listed IT hardware, networking, data-center and power-equipment companies >= $1B in the window, as many as you can find: press releases, 8-K filings, executive changes, activist campaigns, legal settlements, contracts, product launches, guidance, analyst rating/PT changes (firm, old → new), and the stock move. One bullet per company.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **SMTC** `[AI Infrastructure]`
- Semtech raised its fiscal Q3 2027 adjusted EPS outlook to **$1.14 ± $0.02** at its October 15 Data Center Analyst Day; it also presented a fiscal 2030 framework targeting **$3.2 billion** in consolidated net sales, **$2.1 billion** in data-center sales, and fiscal 2026–2030 compound annual growth rates of **38%** and **75%**, respectively. The fiscal 2030 figures were identified as targets, not guidance. (Semtech 8-K, Oct. 15; publication time not stated)[4]

## **CRWV** `[AI Infrastructure]`
- CoreWeave’s shares fell **1.8%** on October 15 after a **15%** decline the prior day; its 2032 bonds traded below **80 cents on the dollar**, while credit-default-swap spreads rose above **1,000 basis points** on October 15 amid concern over leverage and data-center financing. [report] (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not stated)[1][3][5][9]
- CoreWeave’s October 15 stock move was reported at **+6.5%** later in the U.S. session, after the earlier decline; the same report said its 2032 bonds remained below **80 cents on the dollar**. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not stated)[5]

## **ORCL** `[AI Infrastructure]`
- Oracle shares were identified among the AI-linked stocks affected by higher-rate and data-center debt concerns; the stock had fallen **10%** on October 14, while Oracle’s credit-default-swap spreads widened on October 15. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not stated)[1][2][3]

## **DELL / HPE** `[AI Infrastructure]`
- Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares were each reported down **7%** on October 15 during the technology selloff tied to AI-infrastructure financing and higher-rate concerns. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not stated)[5]

## **TSM** `[Fab & Foundry]`
- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported third-quarter net profit of **NT$763.1 billion ($23.59 billion)**, up **69%** year over year and above market forecasts. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not stated)[2]

## **Semiconductors / AI infrastructure** `[Semiconductors]`
- The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell nearly **1%** on October 15, while the Nasdaq Composite rose **0.08%**, the S&P 500 rose **0.33%**, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose **1.08%**; the moves occurred amid concerns about AI spending, data-center demand, and higher financing costs. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not stated)[8]
- The broader technology and semiconductor selloff was associated with higher interest-rate expectations after September U.S. inflation data; Reuters reported that the semiconductor-stock gauge had extended its losing streak to **six sessions** earlier in the period. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not stated)[2][7]
